summary: A transient notification on neutral chrome. Intent is carried by the icon, not by a tinted panel.
useWhen: confirming that something the user just did succeeded or failed
the message is short, transient, and not required to complete a task

useInstead.when: the message must stay until the condition is resolved
useInstead.why: a toast disappears, and anything the user must act on should not

useInstead.when: the message belongs to one field
useInstead.why: Input's error text sits with the field it is about

useInstead.when: you need a decision from the user
useInstead.why: a toast offers one action and takes it away on a timer

neutral.use: a plain fact with no status attached

warning.use: it completed with a caveat worth knowing

error.use: it failed — pair with a way to retry

action.note: exactly one action. A second choice belongs in a Modal, which will still be there

guarantees: auto-dismiss pauses on hover and on focus, and restarts rather than resumes — WCAG 2.2.1, and the forgiving direction
announcement comes from ToastProvider's live region, which is always present rather than appearing with its content
requires: rendering inside a ToastProvider — a Toast on its own is not in a live region
`duration={null}` when the message carries an action the user genuinely needs

antiPatterns.dont: a toast for an error the user must fix
antiPatterns.why: it vanishes; the fix does not
a timed choice is not a choice

antiPatterns.dont: stacking several toasts for one operation
antiPatterns.why: the stack covers the page and the last one is the only one read
